steps.name: Define significant DEG sets from DESeq2 results
caveats: Confirm the actual column names in de_results.csv (e.g. padj vs adj_p_value) before filtering — do not assume exact naming from the profile summary
Use the adjusted p-value (FDR/BH-corrected) column, not raw p-value, for the significance threshold
The low-library sample_01 caveat pertains to the upstream DESeq2 run already performed and delivered; note it in the report but do not attempt to redo DE testing in this step
steps.context: de_results.csv is a DESeq2 results table (12000 genes x 8 columns) for the treated (AD lesional) vs control contrast, 6 vs 6 unpaired design, single batch, from Salmon gene-level counts. Sample sample_01 had a library size ~4x below median but the DE table is already computed (delivered as-is); this step only filters the existing results, it does not re-run DESeq2.
steps.question: Which genes in the treated (AD lesional) vs control DESeq2 contrast pass standard significance thresholds (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1), and what is the full tested background gene set?
acceptance_criteria: Reads de_results.csv (12000 x 8) with columns gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2_fold_change SE/padj etc. as actually present in the file
Produces an up-regulated gene list, a down-regulated gene list, and a combined significant gene list, each with gene symbol/ID and stats
Produces a background gene list = all genes present in de_results.csv with non-NA padj (the tested universe)
Reports counts of up/down/total significant genes and flags if fewer than 10 genes pass threshold (too few for reliable ORA)
Output files (significant gene lists, background list) saved as CSV for the next step

steps.name: GO Biological Process over-representation analysis (ORA)
caveats: Gene ID mapping (symbol -> ENTREZID) can silently drop genes with ambiguous or outdated symbols; report the mapping rate

With only 12000 genes tested (not a full ~20k+ genome-wide count), the background universe should be the actual tested gene set from the counts/DE table, not a default whole-genome background, to avoid inflated significance
n=6 vs 6 unpaired design and the sample_01 low-library-size caveat mean the input DEG list itself carries some uncertainty upstream; note this when interpreting enrichment significance
steps.context: Human (Homo sapiens, taxon 9606) skin RNA-seq, atopic dermatitis lesional vs control, DESeq2 contrast already computed. GO Biological Process gene sets are provided via the locally installed org.Hs.eg.db and GO.db Bioconductor annotation packages (no external GO GMT file is required or present in /mnt/refs; the WikiPathways human GMT in /mnt/refs covers a different pathway database and is not used here).
steps.question: Which GO Biological Process terms are significantly over-represented among the DEGs (up, down, and combined) in the AD lesional vs control skin comparison, relative to the tested gene background?
acceptance_criteria: Runs clusterProfiler::enrichGO (ont='BP') separately for the up-regulated, down-regulated, and combined significant gene sets from T1S1, using the full tested background as the universe
Uses org.Hs.eg.db for GO term-gene mappings and gene ID conversion (map input gene symbols/IDs to ENTREZID/ENSEMBL as required by enrichGO, reporting any genes that fail to map)
Applies BH-adjusted p-value cutoff (q < 0.05) for reporting significant terms, with GO term ID, description, gene ratio, background ratio, adjusted p-value, and member genes
Optionally simplifies redundant GO terms (clusterProfiler::simplify) to reduce parent-child term redundancy
Produces a ranked results table and a summary plot (e.g. dotplot/barplot) of the top over-represented BP terms
If fewer than 10 significant genes were found in T1S1, this step reports that ORA was underpowered/skipped rather than fabricating results

plan.title: GO BP over-representation in AD lesional vs control skin
plan.analytical_narrative: The persisted DESeq2 results table (12000 genes x 8 cols, treated vs control contrast) already contains the differential expression statistics needed to define a significant gene set. The plan (1) loads de_results.csv, applies standard significance thresholds (adjusted p < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1) to define up- and down-regulated gene lists against a background of all tested genes, and (2) runs GO Biological Process over-representation analysis (ORA, hypergeometric test via clusterProfiler::enrichGO) using org.Hs.eg.db as the annotation source, since the organism is human (Homo sapiens, skin, atopic dermatitis lesional vs control). No GO gene-set reference file is required because org.Hs.eg.db (Bioconductor annotation package) and GO.db are installed locally in the sandbox and provide the GO term-gene mappings directly, avoiding dependency on the WikiPathways reference files in /mnt/refs (which cover a different pathway resource, not GO). Results are filtered for redundancy and summarized with the top enriched biological processes, gene ratios, and adjusted p-values, directly answering which GO BPs are over-represented among the significant DEGs.
